rc3 assigns a rollback invariant to each store. Beads, session queue/todos, and root selector are reversible and must return exact captured before-image bytes and SHA-256. The event log is explicitly non-reversible and append-only; compensation must end in MIGRATION_ROLLED_BACK bound to the before-head, committed event hashes, and post-compensation head, returning logical authority to the before-state while bytes advance. Any invariant failure quarantines the migration.

rc3 also closes a normal-consumer read barrier over all four stores before the first commit. Ordinary consumers fail closed with MIGRATION_IN_PROGRESS. Only isolated migration-id-pinned verifiers may read staged or committed state until per-store invariants, cross-store references, zero-authority state, two fresh-worker outputs, and the pre-release receipt validate. Barrier loss triggers rollback/quarantine; the barrier and lease release only after full validation.

The source inventory count is intentionally 825: 501 breadboard entries plus 324 wrapper entries. The added `verify_phase5_v2_fresh_worker_replay.py` is the one-entry increase from the earlier 824 acceptance; rc3 validation requires 825. Catalog remains 49 unchanged items and 1000 points, with zero points/leases/active evidence relations. Review rc3 only; every rc1 and rc2 root remains invalid.

- State/integrity review (`ReviewV2Integrity`): APPROVE. Confirmed per-store rollback semantics, fail-closed ordinary readers across all four stores, actual/recorded `0444` archive modes, two agreeing isolated replay workers, split F7 packet/budget identities, and exact 825 source entries (501 + 324).

Any byte change invalidates both approvals. Both reviewers explicitly invalidate every rc1/rc2 finding or verdict. The approved next authority is a bounded Kyle local-only SPEC_FREEZE. It authorizes only implementation of the reviewed migration transaction; it grants no IBM action, target lease, campaign admission, score, track completion, checkpoint disposition, promotion, or external acceptance.
